settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial online learning with abstention, finite experts (feedback graph G^abs_t)
unmapped: Arms are predictor/abstention pairs (h,r); abstaining incurs a known constant cost c in [0,1] and reveals only losses of abstaining experts, predicting reveals the label and all losses
Learner knows the abstention cost c and the expert set; feedback graph at round t determined by x_t (revealed before acting)
settings.definition_quote: If the inequality $r_{I_t}(x_t) \leq 0$ holds, then the algorithm abstains and incurs as loss an abstention cost $c(x_t) \in [0,1]$. Otherwise, it predicts based on the sign of $h_{I_t}(x_t)$, receives the true label $y_t$, and incurs the loss $\ell(y_t, h_{I_t}(x_t))$.

settings.name_in_paper: Adversarial online learning with abstention, infinite family of Lipschitz expert pairs
unmapped: Comparator class: all pairs (h,r) of L_E-Lipschitz functions X subset R^d -> [-1,1]; X totally bounded with covering number C_X eps^-d
Loss uses ramp 0/1 loss f_gamma with slope 1/(2 gamma); learner knows gamma and the abstention cost c
settings.definition_quote: the class of experts ${\cE} = \set[\big]{\xi = (h, r)\, |\, h, r\colon \cX \subseteq \R^d \to [-1, 1]}$. Here, functions $h$ and $r$ in the definition of $\cE$ are assumed to be $L_{\cE}$-Lipschitz

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic online learning with abstention / time-varying feedback graphs depending on the past
unmapped: z_t=(x_t,y_t) drawn i.i.d. from unknown D; feedback graph G_t at round t depends only on information up to t-1
settings.definition_quote: a stochastic setting (Section \ref{sec:stochastic}), where $z_t$ is assumed to be drawn i.i.d.\ from some unknown distribution $\cD$ over $\cX\times\{\pm 1\}$.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic abstention with feedback graphs not contained in G^sub (lower bound)
unmapped: UCB-NT updates experts according to feedback graphs that are not subgraphs of the subset graph G^sub, producing biased loss estimates
settings.definition_quote: Assume that \UCBNT\ is run with feedback graphs $G_t$ that are not subsets of $\GSUB$.

source.label: th:exp3rej
source.quote: Let \EXPABS\ be run with learning rate $\eta$ over a set of $K$ experts $\xi_1,\ldots,\xi_K$.  Then, the algorithm admits the following regret guarantee after $T$ rounds: \Reg_T(\EXPABS) \leq (\log K)/\eta + \eta\,T (c^2 + 1)/2.

results.notes: Regret defined as sup over experts of expected difference (paper calls it pseudo-regret). Holds for any fixed eta; horizon labelled known since general form uses T only in the bound.

source.label: th:exp3rej
source.quote: In particular, if \EXPABS\ is run with $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{2\log K}{(c^2 + 1)T}}$, then \( \Reg_T(\EXPABS) \leq \sqrt{2(c^2+1)T\log K}. \)

results.notes: Tuned learning rate requires T and c.

symbols.gamma: margin/slope parameter of the ramp loss f_gamma, gamma in (0,1)
symbols.M_T: M*_T(gamma): number of x_t with |r*(x_t)| <= gamma for the best expert (additive term outside the O-tilde)

conditions: h, r are L_E-Lipschitz with values in [-1,1]
X totally bounded with covering number at most C_X eps^-d

source.label: th:infarms
source.quote: If \ContEXPABS\ is run with parameter $\ve \simeq T^{-\frac{1}{2+d}}\,\gamma^{\frac{2}{2+d}}$ and an appropriate learning rate (see Appendix~\ref{app:adversarial}), then, it admits the following regret guarantee: \Reg_T(\ContEXPABS) \leq {\tilde \cO}\left(T^{\frac{d+1}{d+2}}\,\gamma^{-\frac{d}{d+2}}\right) + M^*_{T}(\gamma)

results.notes: M*_T(gamma) is an additive term not inside the O-tilde; the O-tilde hides constants (incl. L_E) and log T factors. Action space mapping (continuum_other) is approximate.

symbols.Phi_cov: E[min over shared admissible coverings C of sum_{C in C} max_{j in C} Delta_j / min_{j in C} Delta_j^2]

conditions: for all t, the feedback graph G_t depends only on information up to time t-1

source.label: th:ucbn
source.quote: Assume that, for all $t \in[T]$, the feedback graph $G_t$ depends only on information up to time $t - 1$.  Then, the regret of \UCBNT\ is bounded as follows: \cO \Bigl( \E \Big[\min_{\cC \in \cF} \sum_{C \in \cC} \frac{\max_{j\in C} \Delta_j}{\min_{j \in C}\Delta_j^2} \log(T) + K \Big] \Bigr )

results.notes: Proof gives explicit constants 20 log T and 5K. Holds for general bounded losses. Corollary 1 specializes to a fixed graph G (min over admissible coverings of G_U, no expectation); not recorded separately. Applies to UCB-NT with the subset graph G^sub.

symbols.Phi_cov: E[min over shared admissible coverings C of the estimated graphs G_t of sum_{C in C} max_{j in C} Delta_j / min_{j in C} Delta_j^2]

conditions: abstention loss with constant abstention cost c
tuning: N_t(j) = {i : hat p_{j,i}^{t-1} <= gamma_{i,t-1}}, gamma_{i,t-1} = sqrt(5 Q_i(t-1) log t)/((K-1)(t-1))

source.label: th:ucbabs
source.quote: For any $t \in [T]$, let the feedback graph $G_t$ be defined by the out-neighborhood $N_t(j) = \set{\xi_i \in \cE \colon \h p_{j, i}^{t -1} \leq  \gamma_{i,t-1 }}$. Then, the regret of \UCBGT\ is bounded as follows: \cO\Bigl( \E \Big[ \min_{\cC \in \cF} \sum_{C \in \cC} \frac{\max_{j\in C }  \Delta_j}{\min_{j \in C }\Delta_j^2} \log(T) + K \Big] \Bigr )

results.notes: Coverings are over UCB-GT's estimated graphs, which contain G^sub.

conditions: algorithm is UCB-NT run with feedback graphs G_t that are not subsets of G^sub
exists a family of predictors H, a Lipschitz loss ell and distribution D (constructed)
holds with arbitrarily high probability p* in (0,1)

source.label: prop:subset
source.quote: Assume that \UCBNT\ is run with feedback graphs $G_t$ that are not subsets of $\GSUB$. Then, there exists a family of predictors $\cH$, a Lipschitz loss function $\ell$ in (\ref{e:absloss}), and a distribution $\cD$ over $z_t$s for which \UCBNT\ incurs linear regret with arbitrarily high probability.

results.notes: Lower bound for a specific algorithm (UCB-NT with non-subset graphs); proof shows regret >= T(mu_j - mu_i) with probability >= p*.
